Problem Statement: The question asks to match different types of AC circuits (purely resistive, L-R series, R-C series, and L-C series) with their correct characteristics regarding how the current relates to the source voltage, specifically whether the current leads, lags, is in phase, or may lead or lag the voltage.

Underlying Concept: The core concept is the phase relationship between current and voltage in AC circuits depending on the circuit elements. In resistors, current and voltage are in phase. In inductors, current lags voltage due to inductive reactance. In capacitors, current leads voltage due to capacitive reactance. In L-C series circuits, inductive and capacitive effects can cancel out, causing current to lead or lag voltage depending on their relative reactances.

Tips and Tricks: Remember the mnemonic: 'ELI the ICE man' where in an Inductor (L), voltage (E) leads current (I), and in a Capacitor (C), current (I) leads voltage (E).
